newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - French May Consumer spending falls.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - French May Consumer spending falls.

text.p: Following are reactions from economists to a 1.1 percent fall in French consumer spending on manufactured goods in May, as reported by national statistics institute INSEE on Thursday.
MARIE OWENS THOMSEN, ECONOMIST, DRESDNER KLEINWORT BENSON:

"It's a bit of a disappointment. That pretty much offsets the April rise and is definitely not a good sign for the second quarter. It means Q2 is looking flat in consumption terms, which will require pretty sharp rise in June to produce a decent Q2.
Although it's worrying, it's not totally out of character. It doesn't perhaps signal any worse weakness than in the past. It doesn't mean consumption will not be an important contributor to growth.
We've had other quite positive numbers such as the 1.1 percent April rise in industrial production, which was more than expected.
It's too early to say the second quarter is going to be a disappointment but it does look like consumption may be weak.
Consumption contributed to 1.4 percent of the 1.5 percent GDP growth last year. So it tends to surprise on the upside.

We forecast consumption contributing 0.9 percent this year, so it still remains one of most important engines of growth but in terms of accelerating contributors we are banking on exports and investment.
The bottom line is that if it is weaker it doesn't matter so much because it cannot be as high as last year. But other (elements) have to pick up.
It's disappointing. The underlying trend is still very weak. There's still uncertainty, due in part to unemployment.
We can expect a bit of pick-up because of the rise in the minimum wage but it's clear there is no big need or desire out there to spend.
We knew growth this year would not rest on consumption. If anything it makes me more comfortable with a 2.0 percent GDP growth forecast for the whole year rather than 2.5 (percent).
But it's a very erratic number. If you have a big positive month, the chances are for negative (one) afterwards.

The economy does need a push to break the domestic demand deadlock. What's clear is we do seem to be in some sort of deadlock. Personally I would orientate more to investment, but you do have to adjust domestic demand.
